lēgŭlēïus , i, m. lex,
I.a pettifogging lawyer, pettifogger, one who depends on legal technicalities for getting the better of his opponent: “leguleius quidam cautus et acutus,” Cic. de Or. 1, 55, 236 : “formularii, vel ut Cicero ait, leguleii,” Quint. 12, 3, 11 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
